# ADR-0058: Lower the SMG frontend in a shared inferlab-gateway-smg package under the backend name smg

> **Status:** accepted | **Date:** 2026-10-03

**References:** [ADR-0022](../adr/ADR-0022.md), [RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md), [RFC-0006](../rfc/RFC-0006.md)

## Context

Two integrations render the SMG frontend. TokenSpeed prefill/decode ([RFC-0003:C-TOKENSPEED-PREFILL-DECODE](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-tokenspeed-prefill-decode)) runs SMG as a fused Gateway and P/D Router over gRPC prefill and decode workers; the Specialized Engine integration runs SMG as the routed-single Gateway in front of one token Engine. Each built the `smg launch` command, readiness, and implementation identity on its own, and the copies diverged: TokenSpeed selected the backend name `tokenspeed-smg`, launched `python3 -m smg launch`, and recorded the adapter version as the implementation version, while the Specialized Engine selected `smg`, launched the `smg` console script, and recorded the installed `tokenspeed-smg` distribution version. Which SMG ran and how it was launched therefore had two authorities. Every observed workspace environment that runs the SMG Gateway installs it from the `tokenspeed-smg` distribution, which provides the `smg` console script. The adapter SDK is framework-neutral and is consumed by every integration.

## Decision

SMG frontend lowering moves into a new workspace-side Python package, `inferlab-gateway-smg`, which depends only on the adapter SDK. It owns the backend name `smg`, used for both the Gateway and the P/D Router, the implementation identity `smg` with the version of the installed `tokenspeed-smg` distribution, the `smg launch` command with the options every SMG frontend shares, the routed-single and prefill/decode target forms, the Gateway readiness probe, and the P/D Router worker-registry readiness that mirrors SMG's `/workers` schema. The integrations keep what their qualification decides: worker commands, routing policy, the public endpoint capabilities they declare, and every other setting. The former TokenSpeed backend name `tokenspeed-smg` is rejected during resolution with a hint to select `smg`, rather than kept as an alias.

## Consequences

Both integrations record the same SMG identity and launch SMG the same way, so a frontend fact recorded for one reads the same for the other, and an SMG launch change lands once. TokenSpeed prefill/decode workspaces must rename `tokenspeed-smg` to `smg` in their Gateway and P/D Router selection; an unrenamed workspace fails resolution with that instruction. TokenSpeed frontend evidence now records the SMG distribution version instead of the adapter version, which the integration identity still records. The release gains one workspace-side wheel, and its first PyPI publication needs a trusted publisher configured for the new project. The SMG engine contract and its protocol identity are not changed by this decision.

## Alternatives Considered

### A shared workspace-side package, inferlab-gateway-smg, that owns the SMG backend name, implementation identity, launch command for routed-single and prefill/decode targets, Gateway readiness, and the P/D Router worker-registry readiness, consumed by both integrations (accepted)

- **Pros:** One authority for the SMG backend name, launch form, and recorded version, Keeps the adapter SDK free of any one frontend implementation's facts
- **Cons:** One more independently versioned package to build, publish, and pin

### Move the shared SMG lowering into the adapter SDK (rejected)

- **Pros:** No new package
- **Cons:** Puts one frontend implementation's command line and registry schema into the framework-neutral SDK every integration consumes

### Keep the two integration-local copies and align them by convention (rejected)

- **Pros:** No change
- **Cons:** The copies have already diverged in backend name, launch form, and recorded version; nothing keeps them aligned
